ai.title: Isolate credentials dir for localhost dev
ai.summary: Refactored credential handling to support isolated directories for local development. The `npm-app` package now imports `userFromJson` and `CREDENTIALS_PATH` from a new local `src/credentials.ts` file instead of `common/src/util/credentials.ts`. This new file constructs the path using `os.homedir()/.config/manicode-${ENVIRONMENT}` when `process.env.ENVIRONMENT` is set and not 'production', preventing dev credentials from clashing with production ones. The shared `common` utility was stripped of these specific path/parse exports.

eli5.text: Starting today, if you run a local development version of the assistant tool, it will read your login credentials from a file named 'manicode-development/credentials.json' inside your computer's hidden config folder, instead of the shared 'manicode/credentials.json' used by the real live service. This keeps your work-in-progress login info from overwriting or mixing with the credentials that the actual deployed assistant uses when you're not actively developing. The change only affects people running a development copy with the ENVIRONMENT variable set; if you just download and use the regular app, nothing looks different to you.

ai.title: Add patch dataset processing scripts and string util
ai.summary: New `scripts/patch-dataset-processing/` directory contains TypeScript utilities for generating AI training datasets from code patches. Scripts handle concatenating raw datasets, processing directory structures, updating patch files to remove trailing context, normalizing sketch comments via `replaceNonStandardPlaceholderComments2`, verifying patches, and creating shuffled JSONL training/validation splits. Core `common/src/util/string.ts` gains `replaceNonStandardPlaceholderComments2` to standardize non-code comments across multiple languages.

eli5.text: You now have new tools that clean up code comments and turn raw code patches into training examples for AI. If you looked, you'd see a new folder of scripts that combine datasets, standardize placeholder comments across languages, verify patches stay consistent, and split results into shuffled practice files. The changes are live today in the developer tooling that prepares future AI training data.

ai.title: Training dataset script filters files over 50,000 tokens
ai.summary: scripts/patch-dataset-processing/create-training-dataset.ts now imports countTokens from backend/util/token-counter and applies a filter dropping entries where countTokens(str) >= 50_000. This prevents oversized conversations from entering the training/validation split. Scope limited to the dataset preparation script; no model, CLI, or Web surface changes. Filter runs post-stringify, pre-shuffle, using a 50_000 token threshold.

eli5.text: If you prepare training data for the assistant, you will no longer include any conversation longer than fifty thousand words, because the preparation tool now skips oversized files before they can corrupt the shuffled training and validation batches. The filter only affects the internal dataset-preparation script, not the running assistant.

ai.title: Refactor ChatStorage class
ai.summary: Refactored `ChatStorage` in `npm-app/src/chat-storage.ts`. Removed unused public methods (`getChat`, `deleteChat`, `listChats`, `setCurrentChat`) and private helpers (`getFilePath`, `generateChatId`), moving remaining private helpers to the end of the class. The `fs` import was dropped as file I/O is stubbed out.

eli5.text: The assistant removed several old features from how chat history is saved, such as the ability to look up, delete, or list past conversations by their ID. If you tried to load or manage a saved chat from a previous session, it would no longer work because the code that did that reading and writing has been stripped out. These changes are internal-only and were never exposed in the visible app, so nothing a regular user sees will behave differently.

ai.title: Replace patch placeholder comments with EXISTINGCODEMARKER
ai.summary: Unified patch generation and sketch updates to use the explicit `EXISTING_CODE_MARKER` constant instead of language-specific comment placeholders. Refactored `replaceNonStandardPlaceholderComments` to accept a mandatory replacement string, removing the legacy multi-pattern regex block. Updated `generatePatch` and `update-sketch.ts` to propagate this marker, ensuring consistent handling of unchanged code sections across backend and tooling.

eli5.text: When the assistant rewrites or shows you a code file with parts left unchanged in the middle, it no longer tries to guess the right comment style for each programming language (like //... for JavaScript or #... for Python). Instead, it uses a single, explicit placeholder marker, '[**REPLACE_WITH_EXISTING_CODE**]', to mark the unchanged sections consistently across all code types and tools. You would notice this only behind the scenes, in how generated code diffs and training data are processed, not in the code you see or write.

ai.title: Add JSX comment pattern to replaceNonStandardPlaceholderComments
ai.summary: Added regex case for JSX comments in `replaceNonStandardPlaceholderComments` in `common/src/util/string.ts`. Matches `{/* ... */}` blocks containing rest/unchanged keywords. Updated `common/src/util/__tests__/string.test.ts` to cover the new pattern.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads your project files, it skips over certain placeholder comments so they don’t get mixed into the parts it actually uses, like examples for training. Previously, it only recognized placeholder comments written in the usual programming style, but now it also recognizes placeholders written in JSX style (the kind used in React or Next.js projects), matching blocks such as {/*... rest */}. This means placeholder comments in JSX files are now left untouched and handled consistently alongside those in other file types. The change is already live in the codebase today.

ai.title: CLI shows usage on quota exceeded
ai.summary: Quota exceeded errors now direct users to the `usage` command. Removed dedicated `quota-exceeded` action; unified error handling via `action-error`. Backend `protec` middleware returns generic error message prompting `usage`. CLI `client.ts` subscribes to `action-error` to display red text and restore prompt.

eli5.text: When you run into a usage limit, the command-line tool now tells you directly how to check your allowance by running the `usage` command, rather than just showing a generic error. The tool lost its own separate message for that specific limit error and now uses a single, consistent error message across the app. You'll notice the error text appears in red and the prompt comes back ready for your next command without you having to do anything extra. No other part of the experience changed for other types of problems.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.87
ai.summary: Updated version to 1.0.87 in `npm-app/package.json`. Routine release increment for the `manicode` package.

eli5.text: If you reinstalled the assistant today, your computer would pull in a newer copy that bundles together a week's worth of recent fixes and additions. The most noticeable thing you'd see is that people who aren't logged in now get a web sign-in button on the login and referrals pages, and the referral system has been tightened so it catches attempts to refer someone who already referred you back. Behind the scenes, the app now keeps its local-development secrets in a separate folder, the websocket connection timeout was increased, and a few dataset-processing scripts were added so the team can keep building AI training data. Everything shipped under a new release label, so the version number on your screen simply reflects a packaged batch of these changes rather than one big new feature.

ai.title: Refine local-only-change detection in generate-patch
ai.summary: Refactored isSketchCompletePrompt in backend/src/generate-patch.ts to better handle Claude's local-only-change detection. Added early returns for EXISTING_CODE_MARKER presence and prior file edits via parseFileBlocks. Updated the GPT-4o classification prompt to explicitly distinguish between REPLACE_ENTIRE_FILE and LOCAL_CHANGE_ONLY, replacing the previous INCOMPLETE_SKETCH logic.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to update just one part of a file (like changing a single function) instead of rewriting the whole file, it now does a smarter check before deciding whether the change looks complete. It first looks for a special marker that signals unchanged code is being kept, if that marker is already there, it trusts your sketch is unfinished and backs off. If the file has never been edited before in this session, it assumes the change is meant to be a full replacement. Otherwise, it asks a more precise question to a helper model: did you intend to replace everything, or are you only touching one piece and expect the rest to stay?
